name: Titmouse Blue
lede: Titmouse Blue is a greenish grey from the Maerz and Paul color dictionary, named for the small songbird rather than for any true blue.

sections.title: A bird that reads grey
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul record Titmouse Blue at #778B86, first dated 1905, on plate 36 F1 of their 1930 dictionary [1]. Despite the name, the ISCC-NBS block built from that plate in 1955 calls it a pale green, not a blue [1]; several titmouse species do carry a blue-grey cap or back, which likely explains the naming even though the books do not spell it out [1].

The nearest named neighbor in our library is [[medici-blue]], a slightly cooler, more saturated grey-blue [1]. The hex value is a screen approximation of an aged dictionary plate [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds this hue, as photographed, in 447 of 23,781 paintings (1.88 percent), more common than 73 percent of the named colors we track [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 32 of 1,674 paintings, at 2.0 times the expected rate for paintings from that century [2]. Inside a painting it most often plays a light, in 38 percent of its 239 occurrences [2].

[[painter:paul-cezanne|Paul Cezanne]] is its most devoted painter here, carrying it in 6 of 50 of his works, 5.5 times his home museums' baseline [2]. The earliest matching painting is dated 1375, 555 years before Maerz and Paul recorded the name in 1930, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. It shares canvases more than chance with [[eucalyptus]] and [[brown-grey]] [2].

origin.named_after: the titmouse, a small songbird with a blue-grey cap on several species
